seen_animation: A black-line hammer (rectangular head, single-stroke handle) in front of a grey scene: a sloped horizon line, a tree trunk at right, zigzag grass at the bottom. Frame 1: the hammer lies nearly horizontal, low and left of the trunk, head at right against the trunk, handle pointing left. Frame 2: it is suddenly high and upright at upper centre, head on top. Frames 3-4: it tips right and moves down-right toward the trunk. Frames 5-10: it holds a diagonal pose, head upper-right touching the trunk's left edge, handle angled down-left. Frames 11-16: the hammer has rotated to a more upright tilt (head up, handle down slightly to the left) and holds there to the end.
seen_film: A bearded caveman sits on a rock beside a dark tree trunk holding a hammer made of a dark stone head bound to a bundle of sticks. Frame 1: he leans forward, hammer swung low to the right striking the rocks. Frame 2: smeared motion as he sits up and lifts the hammer upright near his face. Frames 3-8: he holds the hammer out to his right on a diagonal (head upper-right against the tree edge, handle down-left to his hand) while pressing his other hand to his forehead. Frames 9-10: smears as he brings his hand to his mouth and the hammer starts to swing. Frames 11-16: he holds the hammer more upright in front of him with both hands, head up, handle down, looking dejected; the hammer holds still.
named_subject: A hammer (the caveman's stone-headed hammer), drawn as the doodle's rectangular-head hammer.
evidence: e.png 1 vs f.png 1: hammer low at lower centre-right near the trunk base, as in the film's strike. e.png 2-3 vs f.png 2: hammer raised and upright at upper centre, as the caveman lifts it. e.png 4-8 vs f.png 3-6: hammer tips right into the diagonal held pose with the head against the trunk's left edge; animation settles about 1-2 frames after the film (film settled by 6, animation by 7-8). e.png 8-23 vs f.png 8-23: both hold the diagonal pose. e.png 24-25 vs f.png 24-27: hammer swings to the more upright pose at the same moment the film's smeared swing happens; animation does it in two drawings (24 partial, 25 upright) where the film uses 3-4 smeared frames. e.png 25-38 vs f.png 26-38: both hold the upright pose, head at about one third down the frame, handle down-left. g.png shows one path: frame 1 low, frame 4 high, then a tight cluster for the holds, with no reversal the film lacks. The large change at 1-2 also exists in the film (f.png 1 to 2). Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The frame 1 drawing is proportioned differently from every later drawing (a tall narrow head and a wavy, horizontal handle), so the 1-to-2 change reads as a swap to a different drawing as well as a pose change, and the held diagonal pose sits roughly 10-15% of frame width left of where the film's hammer head is.
closes_when: Frame 1 shows the same wide rectangular head and straight handle proportions as frames 5-38, rotated to point down-right at the rocks, and the held hammer head in frames 7-24 sits slightly further right, overlapping the trunk edge as the film's head does at f.png 6-24.
protect: The timing of the three beats (strike at 1, lift at 2-3, diagonal hold from about 7 to 23, swing to upright at 24-25, upright hold to 38); the steady holds with no drift or jitter; the consistent drawing in frames 5-38 with the rounded top-right head corner and the notch stroke at the top of the handle from c.png; the placement relative to the trunk and horizon.
identity_gap: Frames 2-38 read as the c.png hammer (wide head with one rounded corner, handle with the small notch stroke), but frame 1's head is drawn tall and narrow with a wavy handle, so that one drawing departs from the doodle's proportions.
